newsitem.title: USA: Selfix to triple size with acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Selfix to triple size with acquisition.

text.p: Selfix Inc said Monday it agreed to acquire for cash privately held Tamor Plastics Corp, Leominster, Mass.-based supplier of storage and organization products.
Selfix estimates that the combined entity of Selfix and Tamor would post sales of about $122 million in 1996, or three times the $41 million in sales generated by Selfix in 1995.
Based on the anticipated contribution of the Tamor operations, Selfix said it expects the transaction to add to its net income and earnings per share in 1997 and beyond.
The acquisition is scheduled to close in January 1997.
Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.

Both companies supply product lines to national and regional mass-market retailers. Tamor's products include storage totes, recycling containers, kitchenware, closet organizers and juvenile storage products. Tamor's 1996 sales are expected to be about $80 million. Selfix products include bath, shower and home organization products. Selfix has said it expects 1996 sales of more than $42 million.

"Consolidation among retailers and the vendors who supply them is stratifying our industry," said James Tennant, Selfix chairman and chief executive officer. "Our plan has been to take the lead in this consolidation by acquiring synergistic companies that, when combined, present our customers with the most efficient, highest value way to merchandise their retail operations" he said in a statement.
Selfix also said that Leonard Tocci, 56, will continue as chief executive officer of Tamor, and report to Tennant.
Selfix has manufacturing facilities in Chicago and Hebron, Ill. Tamor operates plants in Leominster, Mass.; Louisiana; Missouri; and Thomasville, Ga.
Trading in shares of Selfix were halted pending an announcement.
